answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil attacks by making identity expensive to rebuild: every account must carry a growing, countersigned history of real work before it earns payment weight. Picture the network as an island with one jetty, and each agent's attestation record as the karst bedrock beneath it. A fresh puppet docks on bare rock and earns nothing until weeks of verified history build its own karst shelf, so one operator spinning up a thousand clones must maintain a thousand shelves. Weight follows demonstrated history, not registration, and mass fakes stay anchored offshore.
